display.purpose: The single largest number on the sheet, in Result Blue; the thing a stranger reads at two metres. Fig 1 only. The token drops to 40px below 860px tall and 46px below 720px wide; the element itself declares font-size once.

headline.purpose: The current pass, with its unit dropped to .46em Ink Two. A clamp, not a token: it scales with the viewport rather than stepping at a breakpoint.

title.purpose: ORBIT in the title block. Used once. The token drops to 20px below 720px wide.

standfirst.purpose: The plain-language question beside the wordmark; the load-bearing clause bolds to 600. Below 720px wide the token resolves to --t-lede rather than to a new step.

readout.purpose: A compared photo's score, with its / 100 denominator dropped to the 11px small tier at 500 Ink Two so the number carries the weight.

body.purpose: Sheet default and the boot message. Tabular numerals so live columns do not shiver.

lede.purpose: Two jobs at one size: the sentence beside the gain figure, and the whole control tier — transport buttons, fields, the speed value, the pass phase pill, score-bar rows, table bodies, the satellite name, the lost-link banner. Absorbed the old 12px and 13px steps, which sat half a pixel apart doing the same job in the same rail.

caption.purpose: Plate captions, control hints, the conditions line, the figure legend, key/value rows, the meter caption, the tooltip, and the sentence-case descriptor in a plate heading.

small.purpose: The dense readout tier: chart and axis text, queue rows, triplet meters, satellite metadata, the ledger lane name at 700/.05em, the sheet tabs at 600/.085em caps, the gain total. Absorbed the old 10.5px step.

label.purpose: Uppercase micro-caps plate and strip headings, plus .micro section labels at .09em; the figure number inside takes Ink at wdth 118%. A caps tier — never used for sentence-case text.

micro.purpose: Chips, honesty tags, rail labels, table heads, the compare who-line, the sent-photo caption, and the ledger lane name past three satellites. A caps tier — letter-spaced caps read optically larger than their pixel size.

mono.purpose: The raw wire trace only; never used for display or UI text.

shadows.name: plate-lift
shadows.purpose: The only elevation token. Every plate, every control group, the lost-link banner. Ambient, never directional.

shadows.name: plate-lift-dark
shadows.purpose: The same token redefined in dark mode.

shadows.name: live-ring
shadows.purpose: Identification, not elevation: the slot happening right now in the ledger, haloed in the plate colour so it survives against its neighbours.

shadows.name: now-segment-ring
shadows.purpose: The current unfilled segment of the contact-window meter.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The system's only easing curve; fast out, long settle.

motion.name: bar-fill
motion.purpose: Score bars and queue rows animate by scaleX on a pre-built element, never by width or rebuild.

motion.name: slot-land
motion.value: land .45s cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1) both — scaleY(.25) and opacity .2 to full
motion.purpose: A newly awarded slot cell landing in the ledger.

motion.name: pass-lamp-breathe
motion.value: breathe 1.9s cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1) infinite — opacity 1 to .35, scale 1 to .82
motion.purpose: The only looping animation in the system; marks a pass that is open right now.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: all animations and transitions clamped to .001ms under prefers-reduced-motion

breakpoints.name: short
breakpoints.purpose: --t-hero to 40px, satellite thumbnails 96px to 84px, grid rows tighten.

breakpoints.name: shorter
breakpoints.purpose: Drops the sent-photo strip and the compare caption; nothing shrinks.

breakpoints.name: scroll-escape
breakpoints.purpose: The page starts scrolling and fixed rows become content-sized, rather than clipping a figure in half.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: Two-column stack in source order; plates stop clipping; the page scrolls.

Fig 1 Useful imagery delivered, same photos, same window

Plate content.

components.name: Transport Button

components.css: .ds-transport { display: flex; gap: 3px; } .ds-btn { font: 600 12.5px/1.4 Archivo, system-ui, sans-serif; color: var(--ink, #11161b); background: var(--plate-sunk, #f4f6f8); border: 1px solid var(--rule-soft, #e2e8ed); border-radius: 3px; padding: 5px 11px; cursor: pointer; white-space: nowrap; transition: background-color .14s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), border-color .14s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), color .14s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); } .ds-btn:hover { border-color: var(--rule, #c9d2da); background: var(--stock, #edf0f3); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--blue, #1b54c8); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn[aria-pressed="true"] { background: var(--ink, #11161b); border-color: var(--ink, #11161b); color: var(--plate, #fff); } .ds-btn:disabled { opacity: .4; cursor: default; }

components.name: Control Group
components.description: A labelled cell of the single control rail: 9.5px caps label, 11.5px hints, 12.5px fields, on a white plate-let.

components.name: Sheet Tabs
components.description: The three sheets of the report, on the 11px small step. The selected tab inverts to Ink; there is no underline or indicator bar.

components.css: .ds-meter { font: 400 14px/1.4 Archivo, system-ui, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-phase { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; margin-bottom: 9px; font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .02em; padding: 4px 10px 4px 8px; border-radius: 3px; background: rgba(192,39,31,.10); border: 1px solid transparent; color: var(--red, #c0271f); } .ds-lamp { width: 9px; height: 9px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--red, #c0271f); flex: none; animation: ds-breathe 1.9s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) infinite; } @keyframes ds-breathe { 0%,100% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); } 50% { opacity: .35; transform: scale(.82); } } .ds-track { height: 20px; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--plate-sunk, #f4f6f8); border: 1px solid var(--rule-soft, #e2e8ed); display: flex; gap: 2px; padding: 2px; overflow: hidden; } .ds-track i { flex: 1 1 0; border-radius: 1px; background: var(--rule-soft, #e2e8ed); transition: background-color .25s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); } .ds-track i[data-used] { background: var(--blue, #1b54c8); } .ds-track i[data-now] { background: var(--rule-soft, #e2e8ed); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--red, #c0271f); } .ds-cap { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px; font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--ink-2, #4e5a66); margin-top: 5px; } .ds-cap b { color: var(--ink, #11161b); font-weight: 700; }

narrative.overview:
Orbit is a semiconductor datasheet and test-report spread that happens to be updating ten times a second. Every quantity on the sheet carries a plain-English name, a unit, and how we know it; anything nobody has measured says so in the same breath, in the same size type, without apology. The surface is cool bond stock (#edf0f3) carrying white plates (#ffffff), hairline rules doing nearly all the separation, and Archivo alone across the whole ramp — width axis for plate headings and big figures, weight and size for everything else.

The density is high and deliberately unpadded: a 9–12px rhythm, 9.5–12.5px supporting type, and figures that jump to 34–54px so a stranger two metres away reads the gain before they read anything else. Nothing is decorative. There is no hue that does not mean something, no icon, no gradient, no glass, no neon. The build explicitly refuses the mission-control console with green-on-black telemetry that every space demo ships, and the rounded-card dashboard it replaced.

Elevation is one token and one token only (--sh), a two-stop ambient lift carried by every plate and control group. It is diffuse, near-invisible in isolation, and it exists to separate a white plate from a nearly-white stock where a 1px rule alone read as a seam. It is not a card shadow: there is no hard offset, no hover lift, and no second step. A future surface that wants depth reuses this token or goes without.
keyCharacteristics: Cool bond stock, white plates, hairline rules, 3px corners at the largest.
Five semantic pens, each with exactly one job; no sixth pen may be invented.
Archivo variable alone, width axis carrying the datasheet voice.
A closed type ramp: seven literal steps and four responsive tokens.
Every figure is named, united, and tagged measured / modelled / failed.
One screen above 1180×759; panels clip, the page never does.
Fully self-hosted — no CDN font, script, or image, enforced by the build.

rules.name: The Five Pens Rule
rules.body: Blue, pencil, red, green, amber. Each has exactly one job: result, baseline, live-or-forced, measured, modelled. A new colour is a new claim, and there are no more claims to make. Never add a sixth pen, and never borrow an existing pen for a meaning it does not already carry.

rules.name: The Numbered Lane Rule
rules.body: A satellite is identified by its lane position and its number, never by a hue. This is what lets the ledger show twelve satellites without generating twelve colours, and what keeps blue meaning "Orbit's result" in a panel full of satellites. Never assign a per-satellite colour.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: The baseline curve is dashed as well as grey; the window-saturation line is dashed as well as amber; a live slot gets a ring as well as red. Any distinction carried by one of the five pens must also be carried by a second channel — dash, ring, weight, or position.

rules.name: The Ink-Only Rule
rules.body: A colour value in this build is always ink. The two overflow masks on the queue and the sent-photo strip are written with the black keyword precisely because they are alpha channels, not paint — reading them as an undocumented colour token would be the mistake they are written to prevent.

rules.name: The Closed Ramp Rule
rules.body: Seven literal steps and four tokens are the whole ramp. A new surface picks the nearest existing step; it does not add one. If two steps would sit within half a pixel of each other doing the same job, they are the same step — that is how 13px and 12px were absorbed into 12.5, and 10.5 into 11.

rules.name: The One Declaration Rule
rules.body: A role that changes size at a breakpoint owns a :root token (--t-hero, --t-title, --t-lede, --t-standfirst) and exactly one font-size declaration. Media queries override the token, never the element. Never reintroduce a per-breakpoint font-size on a component.

rules.name: The Caps Tier Rule
rules.body: 9.5 and 10px exist only as uppercase, letter-spaced type; 11 and 11.5px exist only as sentence-case text. Letter-spaced caps read larger than their pixel size, so the two pairs are separate tiers and swapping one for the other inverts the hierarchy. Never set a caps label at 11px or body text at 10px.

rules.name: The Width-Axis Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is carried by size and weight; the width axis is carried by role. Figures and headings widen (106–118%); nothing else touches font-stretch. Never substitute a second family for emphasis — Archivo is the only face on the sheet.

rules.name: The Named Quantity Rule
rules.body: Every number on the sheet appears with a plain-English name a non-specialist can read, its unit in Ink Two beside it, and a provenance tag. "Photos scored per second · photos/s · MEASURED at 100 MHz", never a bare number under an acronym.

rules.name: The One Screen Rule
rules.body: Above 1180px wide and 759px tall the live sheet fits the viewport with body { overflow: hidden }. Panels clip their own overflow — the queue fades out under a 9px mask, the sent-photo strip under a 22px horizontal mask — and the page never scrolls. Below 759px tall the page is allowed to scroll on purpose. Audit test: at 1440×800, nothing on sheet 1 is reachable by scrolling, and no figure is cut.

rules.name: The Drop, Don't Shrink Rule
rules.body: When height runs out, whole secondary elements are removed by media query and the primary ones keep their size. Never solve a height squeeze by shrinking the gain figure below 40px or the queue below 38px.

rules.name: The One Elevation Rule
rules.body: There is a single shadow token and it is ambient. Never introduce a second elevation step, a hover lift, a directional or hard offset shadow, or a shadow on anything smaller than a plate.

rules.name: The Matched Radius Rule
rules.body: A fill takes the radius of the well it sits in: the score-bar fill is 5px because its track is 5px, not because 4px looked close enough. Never invent a radius step for an inner element.

rules.name: The Round Number Rule
rules.body: niceScale picks the axis step from 0.1/0.2/0.25/0.5/1/2/2.5/5 × a power of ten, keeps 3–7 steps, and among the candidates keeps the one clearing the peak with the least headroom — an axis towering over the data flattens the very gap the figure exists to show. Then it labels every ⌈ticks/4⌉th line so labels breathe. Never hand-pick an axis maximum.

rules.name: The Built Once Rule
rules.body: The DOM is constructed once and updated in place on the 10 Hz tick — text content, attributes, and transform: scaleX() on a bar fill with a .3s ease. Never re-render a live region with innerHTML on tick, and never create an before a real corpus frame exists for it. This is why the display does not flicker while a judge is reading it.

dos: Do give every pen exactly one job: blue = Orbit's result, pencil = the baseline, red = live or forced, green = measured on hardware, amber = modelled or not yet measured.
Do identify satellites by numbered lane and position, so the display scales to twelve without inventing hues.

Do pair a provenance tag with every figure — measured (green) with where it was measured, estimate / modelled (amber) with what the model assumed, and the literal not measured yet where no number exists.
Do carry any distinction in a second channel besides colour: the baseline is dashed as well as grey, the live slot is ringed as well as red.
Do pick the nearest existing step on the ramp — 9.5, 10, 11, 11.5, 12.5, 14, 19px, or one of the four --t- tokens.
Do give a role that resizes at a breakpoint a :root token and one font-size declaration, and override the token in the media query.
Do keep 9.5 and 10px for uppercase letter-spaced type and 11 and 11.5px for sentence case; the caps tiers read larger than their number.
Do keep the live sheet on one screen above 1180×759 — clip inside panels, with a mask fade, and let the page scroll only below 759px tall.
Do write mask gradients with the black keyword, so an alpha stop is never mistaken for a colour token.
Do set the SVG viewBox to the box's pixel size so one unit is one pixel.
Do build the DOM once and update text, attributes and scaleX() in place on the 10 Hz tick.
Do self-host every asset under viz/static/ — tools/offline_check.py fails the build on any https:// reference from index.html.
Do set plate headings and large figures on the width axis (106–118%) and leave everything else at the default width.
donts: Don't invent a sixth pen, or reuse one of the five for a meaning it does not already carry.
Don't give a satellite its own colour, ever.
Don't print a number without a plain-English name, a unit, and a provenance tag — a bare figure reads as measured whether it is or not.
Don't add a type step. If a size sits within half a pixel of an existing step doing the same job, it is that step.
Don't put a font-size on a component inside a media query; override the role's --t- token instead.
Don't add a second elevation step, a hover lift, or a directional or hard offset shadow; there is one ambient shadow token and it applies to plates.
Don't reach for a second typeface, an icon font, or a glyph icon; Archivo and drawn SVG marks are the whole vocabulary.
Don't solve a height squeeze by shrinking the gain figure or the queue — drop a secondary element instead.
Don't give an inner fill a different radius from the well it sits in.
Don't rebuild a live region with innerHTML on the tick, or create image elements for frames that do not exist yet.
Don't link a font, script, or image from a CDN.
Don't round a corner past 3px (5px on bar tracks) or introduce a gradient, glow, or green-on-black telemetry styling; this is a test report, not a console.
